newsitem.title: UK: Dollar supports European soft oils, palm unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Dollar supports European soft oils, palm unchanged.

text.p: A firm dollar against major European currencies underpinned soft oil prices on the European vegetable oil market on Tuesday.
However, traders said buyers were not rushing to follow.
"Buyers have moved up a bit but they are not close to the sellers yet," said a trader.
Traders said the higher close in Chicago on Monday was not a major influence on the market.
"People are looking at currency, not Chicago," said another trader.

Palm oil sellers were little changed from Monday in a lightly traded market. Rangebound futures in Kuala Lumper gave European traders little to go on and at midday crude palm oil cif Europe was unchanged with buyers $2.50 to $7.50 below the asking price.
RBD palm oil was unchanged to $2.50 up after Apr traded at $540 and May at $535 and $536.50 a tonne fob Malaysia ports.
Olein was also unchanged to $2.50 higher after dated Apr fetched $576.50, May $577.50 and Jun $567.50 a tonne.
Coconut oil offers were $2.50 to $7.50 higher while palmkernel oil was mixed at $2.50 up to $2.50 down.
Dutch soy oil offers were around 1.50 to 2.50 guilders up while rape oil was one to 1.25 guilders higher.
